items.note: Association named, organized at Larrow Green 1889, creamery 1891; Gideon Vose as first president absent from Section A, but this is a >2-bold list with no REQUIRED line and the core fact is present
'By-law Article Seven stipulated payment by tested butterfat content, not milk weight'; the 'test of the station where he delivers governs' clause is absent but core fact carries

The station-gain ledger line appears only in Section D; credit does not travel into Section A
Ostrey Hollow skimming station, seven miles up, built 1895-96, opened 4 May 1896; borrowed Larrow Green glass not stated but core fact carries
Weighed in, sampled, tested, cream hauled to Larrow Green, skim returned; Story 2 adds the short charge into a bottle ruled for a full charge
Ammon & Sons of Tarnet, in use 1 May 1897; the 14 April invoice date sits in Section C only, but core fact carries

'0.19 percentage points, flat as a floor, through wet years and dry, summer and winter'

No summary leaf: no 1896 figure of 3.80 beside 3.61 from 1898, no step at the change of glassware
8 May 1911 breakage, borrowed measure, nine weeks to 10 July, tests rose and fell back on resumption
Married Orra Brant, Emmet's sister; Emmet the largest patron

1908 committee mentioned but not under Nyle Grigg and without the January-March sampling window

No descent of the weigh book to Roy Brant in 1929 or its loan to Ivy in 1958

No 0.19 higher in every overlapping season, no sixteen seasons 1915-1930

Ran the lactometer at every circuit visit and never found added water at the station

'His entry was brief and factual; it contained no backward-looking commentary'; no one connected the condemnation to the prior decades

No account of assembling records that had never been in the same room
February 1958, crate found in the station loft, nine surviving pipettes

67,000 lb and $19,600, and no ledger identity with the station-gain total; all four REQUIRED elements fail

Granddaughter, correct

Second cousins with full derivation

Gideon Vose, his father, correct

$77.93 with line items; $77.39 named only as a rejected discrepancy

Variable named as the pipette / measuring glass
Herds, pasture and season, separator, men, same tester - more than three constants
Nine weeks, 8 May to 10 July, tests rose and fell back the day the station's own glass returned; the 3.80/3.61 figures are missing but the result is stated and the nine weeks is right
States the cause lies in the glass, not herds, pasture, procedure or honesty, and states limits (it does not size the error; that came only from 1958)

Argues independence by evidentiary level and states all three would hold without the 1958 measurement

Answers the literal question yes, citing the 1902 complaints and the 1919 circular

Only two of five established facts (signed ledger sheets carrying the gain, the 1919 circular). Manager year wrong (1911); never says he argued watering at the hearing; never notes that nothing in his hand names the glassware. REQUIRED three

A04 touched only inside Section A and leans to r20's reground-mold pole; A06 and A10 never raised

A05: asserts 'Ansel Keddie suspected the glass' on Duncan's single uncorroborated recollection
